Camila / Marissa —

Summary of technical constraints and recommended flows for FintechCo: 

1) Live data and caches:
- We can remove PII from the primary serving store and invalidate KV/prefix caches within 24 hours of a validated request.

2) Backups / snapshots:
- Our default snapshot cadence is daily snapshots retained for 90 days with a 7-day immediate restore window. Snapshots are incremental and encrypted.
- We do not perform "physical overwrite" on immutable cloud snapshots. Two practical options: 
  a) Crypto-delete: rotate the encryption keys for the specific snapshot set to render data unrecoverable. That is achievable but requires coordination with owner-managed KMS in Private deployments; for Hosted, we can perform key rotation on our managed KMS and mark snapshots as crypto-expired. Crypto-deletion timeline: typically 7-30 days depending on key rotation and downstream replication.
  b) Delayed purge on snapshot expiry: if snapshot TTL is 90 days, data will be gone after TTL; for acceleration we can take targeted snapshots and delete earlier but this depends on provider API limitations and any legal hold.

3) Logs / telemetry:
- We support PII filtering at ingest (regex/structured) for common PII types; retrospective redaction is possible in our log indexer but is best-effort and can be slow for large volumes. Retrospective redaction timeline: 1-14 days depending on index size.

4) Downstream notifications:
- Recommended pattern: emit an RTBF event to a webhook endpoint and provide an export (CSV/JSON) with deletion ids. We can also push to a customer-managed S3 bucket or Kafka topic for CDC. Webhook retries, signing, and idempotency keys are supported.

5) Legal hold: if a user is subject to legal hold, we will mark the record as "in litigation" and defer physical purge until hold is released; we can provide retention audit logs for requests.

Caveats: Hosted customers have less control over KMS for crypto-delete; Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) can use customer KMS/HSM for stronger assurances. Backups replicated to other regions may extend the window for crypto-deletion.

Let me know if you want a short diagram or a step-by-step runbook.

- Logs: We offer PII redaction at ingest; retrospective redaction is possible but may take up to 14 days for large indexes. We can provide a scoped quote if you need faster turnaround.
- Downstream notifications: We can push RTBF events to a webhook, S3, or Kafka. We recommend webhook + S3 export for robust downstream reconciliation.
- Legal hold: will defer deletion per your process; we will provide audit logs showing attempted actions and hold flags.
